None of the three proposed answers is correct, because a permutation-invariant distance-2 code with q = 3 exists on n = 4 qudits. All three solutions give a larger minimum for q = 3 (Solution 1: 6; Solutions 2 and 3: 5).

**Reduction.** For symmetric codewords, ⟨ψ_a|E_i|ψ_b⟩ is the same for every site i, so the Knill–Laflamme conditions for single-qudit errors reduce to one-body operators a_j†a_k (second quantization). Writing |k⟩ for occupation vectors k with Σk_i = n, the requirement is:
- ⟨ψ_a|a_j†a_k|ψ_b⟩ = 0 for a ≠ b and all j, k;
- ⟨ψ_a|a_j†a_k|ψ_a⟩ is independent of a.

**Explicit q = 3, n = 4 code.** Use the all-even occupation states |400⟩, |040⟩, |004⟩, |220⟩, |202⟩, |022⟩, with |220⟩ denoting the normalized symmetric state on {1,1,2,2}:

- ψ₁ = √(1/3)|004⟩ + √(2/3)|220⟩
- ψ₂ = √(1/3)|040⟩ + √(2/3)|202⟩
- ψ₃ = √(1/3)|400⟩ + √(2/3)|022⟩

Checks:
- **Orthonormal:** each has norm 1, and the three use disjoint occupation sets.
- **Hops vanish:** a_j†a_k (j ≠ k) changes two occupations by ±1, producing odd entries. Every codeword is supported on all-even occupations, so all hop matrix elements are zero, including the diagonal ones.
- **Equal one-body populations:** ⟨n₁⟩ = ⟨n₂⟩ = ⟨n₃⟩ = 4/3 for each codeword. Hence ⟨E₁⟩ = 1/3 for E = |j⟩⟨j| in every codeword.
- **Cross terms vanish:** the diagonal cross terms vanish by disjoint supports.

So this is a 3-dimensional symmetric code with distance at least 2 on 4 qudits. Since 4 < 5 < 6, none of the three claimed minima for q = 3 can be the true minimum.

CHOICE: NONE
